method: Two actually inspected ordinary front/aerial photographs and current standard PMTiles. No bespoke archival,survey or doorway research.

references.observed: Actually inspected official ordinary waterfront exterior. The historic palace is a compact long stone block with two tall ornamental window stories above a low rusticated basement, shallow gray/green hipped roofs, deep cornices/attic band, repeated paired slender columns/pilasters and original layered curved window-head shapes. Slightly projecting groups divide the waterfront facade. A raised entrance/balcony and divided exterior stair occur at the southwestern short end. Waterfront garden gates, quay, helipad and bridge are independent context. Do not copy figurative carving or inscriptions.

Actually inspected broad daytime aerial. The compact historic principal palace has connected complete roof volumes and is separate from the modern multi-wing hotel to its east. A lower separate building connects estate context behind/between the two,while gardens,pool,seawall and marina-side structures remain separate. No clear open roof court is visible in this image; the standard native principal polygon has no inner hole. The image establishes relative site scope and roof composition,not exact roof details or surveyed heights.
